verifications.claim: Cancer is a group of diseases characterized by uncontrolled cell growth caused by DNA alterations.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'body cells grow uncontrollably... caused due to DNA mutation'; R4: 'class of diseases characterized by out-of-control cell growth'; R17: 'group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly describe cancer as diseases with uncontrolled cell growth due to DNA mutations/alterations.

verifications.claim: Uncontrolled cell growth in cancer results in tumors or blood cancers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'grow uncontrollably, forming a lump of tissues or tumor'; R4: 'form lumps or masses of tissue called tumors (except... leukemia)'; R13: 'extra cells can form a mass called a tumor'
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for tumors from uncontrolled growth, and exception for blood cancers like leukemia.

verifications.claim: Cancer can spread (metastasize).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'spreading into different organs'; R2: 'spread to other body organs... metastasized'; R5: 'spread to other organs; the latter process is referred to as metastasis'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Cancer is diagnosed through imaging, biopsies, and blood tests.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R13: 'blood tests or imaging tests... biopsy is typically the only way to confirm'; R6: 'Imaging... Biopsies... Blood tests'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported as common diagnostic methods.

verifications.claim: Cancer is treated with surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Surgery... Radiation therapy... Chemotherapy'; R17: 'Radiation therapy, surgery, chemotherapy'
verifications.reasoning: Standard treatments explicitly listed.

verifications.claim: CT scans, MRIs, PET scans, and X-rays are commonly used imaging tests for cancer diagnosis, notes the Mayo Clinic.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: Specific list and Mayo Clinic attribution not present in any reference.

verifications.claim: Biopsy involves taking a small sample of tissue for examination, says MedlinePlus.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R13: 'A biopsy is the procedure of removing and examining tissue, cells, or fluids from your body'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match from MedlinePlus.

verifications.claim: Biopsy is a definitive method for cancer diagnosis, says MedlinePlus.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R13: 'A biopsy is typically the only way to confirm a cancer diagnosis'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated as confirmatory by MedlinePlus.

verifications.claim: Laboratory tests for cancer include blood or urine tests that look for specific cancer cells or tumor markers, according to MedlinePlus.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R13: 'Blood tests... Specific proteins and hormones... Urinalysis: ... proteins in your urine'
verifications.reasoning: Matches blood/urine tests for markers/cells.

verifications.claim: Endoscopy procedures and physical exams are used to look inside the body and detect abnormalities for cancer diagnosis, explains National Cancer Institute.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R6: 'Endoscopy: ... get an up-close look at organs, tissues'; R13: 'Do a physical exam'
verifications.reasoning: Supported generally, but no direct NCI attribution or exact phrasing.

verifications.claim: Cancer surgery involves removing the tumor, says Wikipedia.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R16: 'remove cancer from the body... remove cancerous tissue'; R17: 'surgery typically attempts to remove the entire mass'
verifications.reasoning: Direct description matches.

verifications.claim: Chemotherapy uses drugs to kill cancer cells, according to Wikipedia.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'anti-cancer drugs to destroy cancer cells'; R17: 'chemotherapy... cytotoxic anti-neoplastic drugs'
verifications.reasoning: Precise match.

verifications.claim: Radiation therapy uses high-dose radiation to kill cancer cells, notes Wikipedia.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'uses high doses of radiation to kill fast-growing malignant cells'; R17: 'ionizing radiation... to kill malignant cells'
verifications.reasoning: Exact description.

verifications.claim: Targeted therapy and immunotherapy for cancer target specific genetic changes or boost the immune system, explains Wikipedia.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Targeted therapies: ... specific molecular pathways'; R17: 'targeted therapy... immunotherapy'
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for mechanisms.

verifications.claim: CAR-T cell therapy engineers a patient's own T-cells to attack cancer, says a YouTube video from the National Cancer Institute.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R11: 'doctors extract T-cells from... genetically engineering them... identify and target cancer cells'
verifications.reasoning: Precise match to CAR-T description.

verifications.claim: Precision medicine involves developing treatments tailored to the specific genetic makeup of a tumor, notes the World Health Organization.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Precision medicine... select treatments... based on a genetic understanding of their disease'
verifications.reasoning: Supported in R4, but not attributed to WHO (R5 mentions targeted therapies vaguely).

verifications.claim: Tobacco use is the leading cause of cancer, says Cancer Progress Report.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Tobacco use is the leading preventable cause of cancer'
verifications.reasoning: R3 (Cancer Progress Report) specifies 'leading preventable cause', not overall leading cause.

verifications.claim: Tobacco use accounts for a significant portion of cancer deaths, says Cancer Progress Report.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Tobacco use is the leading preventable cause of cancer... exposes individuals to many harmful chemicals'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supports significant portion via leading preventable cause.

verifications.claim: Cancer risk factors from lifestyle and environment include obesity, poor diet, lack of exercise, alcohol, and UV radiation, say Wikipedia and the VCU Massey Comprehensive Cancer Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'excess body weight, alcohol, poor diet, and physical inactivity... ultraviolet radiation'; R10: 'high-fat diet... UV radiation'; R17: 'obesity, poor diet, lack of physical activity, excessive alcohol, UV'
verifications.reasoning: Exact list matches across sources including Massey (R10).

verifications.claim: Viruses such as HPV and Hepatitis are risk factors for cancer, according to the World Health Organization.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5 (WHO): 'human papillomavirus (HPV) and hepatitis... carcinogenic infections'; R3: 'HPV... hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV)'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported by WHO (R5).
